requirements.requirement: Establish a filesystem snapshot mechanism for /srv/data on node1 with application data populated so it can be captured for recovery
requirements.summary: No pre-existing LVM/Btrfs was found on node1 (single XFS root, no spare disk), so the executor built a loopback-backed LVM PV/VG/LV, formatted XFS, mounted persistently at /srv/data via fstab, and populated it with application config and 20 record files. A sha256 baseline manifest was captured directly confirming the data was in place before any snapshot was taken.

requirements.requirement: Take a filesystem snapshot before modification, modify the directory, then restore the exact content captured by the earlier snapshot
requirements.summary: An LVM COW snapshot (data_snap) was created from the populated LV. /srv/data was then modified (two files deleted, config tampered, one file overwritten, a rogue file added), with a sha256 diff directly showing the divergence from baseline. `lvconvert --merge` was then used to roll the origin LV back to the snapshot state, the LV was reactivated and remounted, and a fresh sha256 manifest diff against the original baseline showed zero differences ('RESTORE VERIFIED: content matches baseline exactly'), directly confirming exact content recovery.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task — establishing a snapshot-capable filesystem for /srv/data and demonstrating an exact restore from a pre-modification snapshot — are directly and fully evidenced via LVM PV/VG/LV creation, sha256 baseline capture, deliberate corruption, and a byte-for-byte-verified lvconvert --merge restore. The separately mandated node-restart evidence protocol was also completed cleanly: pre-restart boot_id/health baseline, systemctl reboot, changed boot_id post-reboot, and recovered loop device/LVM/mount/data state matching baseline exactly, cross-checked by the fixed before-prepare and after-executor boot-identity snapshots (cce73776... -> 182fdfdf...). No unnecessary mutations, failed services, or unsafe exposure were introduced.
limitations: The restart protocol is independent of the public task contract; it was completed with strong direct evidence but is not itself a material task outcome, so it does not affect the requirement scores above.
A handful of temporary sha256 diff files were left under /tmp; this is minor and does not affect functional correctness of the task.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map clearly to the task: building the LVM-backed snapshot infrastructure and populating data (cmd-1d5bb16d6f254633), taking the snapshot and deliberately corrupting data to prove restoration (cmd-7bb79ae054a74e49), restoring via lvconvert --merge (cmd-5a5b71ca12334f93), and the separately mandated restart-evidence protocol (cmd-cb5624144357431a, cmd-f26ca69901ff4b1c, cmd-b4b70342bdee432e, cmd-816e04b849984a00). No unnecessary or unexplained mutations, failed services, or unsafe exposure were found; the after_executor lifecycle snapshot shows no new failed services and the listening-socket set is unchanged (only PIDs differ post-reboot, as expected). Minor residue: four small sha256 diff files (/tmp/post-modify.sha256, /tmp/post-restore.sha256, /tmp/pre-restart.sha256, /tmp/post-reboot.sha256) were left in /tmp — low-risk, bounded evidence artifacts rather than abandoned experiments, but not cleaned up.
